newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius stock index rises for seventh session.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius stock index rises for seventh session.

text.p: The Mauritius Stock Exchange share index Semdex rose 1.71 points to 328.05 on Monday as prices followed their November rise, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 4.86 million rupees on 283,486 shares from 9.24 million rupees on 364,670 shares last Friday.
Market analysts said the Mauritius bourse was continuing a correction after prices fell in September and October because of political uncertainty.

"Until recently, the question was what would turn the market from its depressed levels. We now have an answer. The new question which is being asked now is until when this correction will last," a market analyst said.

The establishment of a new country fund which would invest $20 million in the stock market from early 1997 halted a streak of 19 consecutive trading sessions of falling share prices and lifted the bourse from its year's low in late October.
The Semdex rose for its seventh straight session on Monday.
But analysts say an upcoming government cabinet reshuffle could be a serious test for the market.
"Without any doubt, the market's fate now lies in the hands of the reshuffle. It will strongly reflect how the private sector will view the new finance minister," the analyst added.
Shares continued to rise on Monday as investors were taking advantage of good buying opportunities, bourse officials said. No stocks lost ground on Monday.
Conglomerate Rogers posted a gain of one rupee to 89.50 rupees on 6,000 shares and oil company Shell (Mauritius) rose 20 cents to 13.50 rupees on 4,213 shares.

Horse racing betting firm Automatic Systems Limited (ASL) was 1.10 rupees higher to 29.90 on 350 shares. ASL is expected to show good financial results this year as good crowd figures were reported at race meetings in Mauritius this year.
Hotel stocks Sun Resorts gained 40 cents to 36 rupees on 8,651 shares and Grand Baie Hotel was 30 cents higher to 35 rupees on 1,130 shares.
In the banking sector, Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 73 rupees on 7,612 shares and State Bank of Mauritius was stable at 8.70 rupees on 143,700 shares.
Building blocks manufacturer United Basalt Products climbed 80 cents to 27 rupees on 100 shares.
Investment based Promotion And Development (PAD) rose 50 cents to 15.50 rupees on 18,125 shares and General Investment and Development Company (ordinary) added 20 cents to 5.50 rupees on 300 shares.
Sugar stock Mon Tresor Mon Desert edged up by 10 cents to 37.10 rupees on 2,302 shares and Happy World Foods traded 7,694 shares at 15.10 rupees from 15.00 rupees on Friday.
